$comment: Declaration for scripts/verify/release-drift.sh — edit THIS, never the
script's internals, so there is exactly one place a number lives.
WHY THIS EXISTS. On 2026-09-02 `main` was 1,242 commits past the v2.18.0
tag (441 fix, 112 feat) with the workspace version STILL reading 2.18.0.
Nothing anywhere said so. `version-lockstep` was green the whole time —
correctly, because it only checks that tauri.conf.json, Cargo.toml and
community main agree WITH EACH OTHER, and three files agreeing on a stale
version is exactly as true after 1,242 commits as before. The release
machinery was never broken; a release was simply never started, because the
version on main equalled the last released version and no gate cared.
This measures the thing that actually drifted.
$why_threshold: 250 separates two named outcomes. Below it: a normal release cadence — the
gaps between v2.16.x and v2.18.0 were tens of commits, not hundreds. Above
it: a release that has been forgotten rather than deferred, which is the
state this exists to surface. It is a DECLARED assumption, written here so a
reader can disagree with a specific number rather than an invisible one.
$why_grandfather: Current drift is far past the threshold, and a gate that fails every PR on
day one is a gate the first person it blocks disables — the override habit
forms because an instrument is unactionable, not because it is loud
(instrument-discipline.md MUST-1). So until this date the gate WARNS loudly
and exits 0; after it, drift past the threshold FAILS.
This is the calendar backstop from completion-criterion.md MUST-6: an
event trigger that never fires parks forever, so the deferral has a date on
it. Cutting the release is what clears this — not moving the date. Moving it
